header.name: Advanced Solid-state Devices (ASD)
header.description: This course will cover the fundamental principles of diode, MOSFET, and BJT, and will also explain advanced concepts related to these devices, such as non-ideal effects. It will develop an understanding that will be useful in designing semiconductor-based circuits and systems. This course will also cover advanced solid-state devices that will help students undertake device-centric research in the future.
prerequisites_mandatory: Physics of Semiconductor Devices (UG) and equivalent for PG
prerequisites_mandatory_resolved: Physics of Semiconductor Devices (UG) and equivalent for PG

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Clearly explains operating principle and terminal characteristics of diodes, MOSFET and BJT, including non-ideal effects.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Is able to compute a given parameter or physical quantity for pn junction, MOSFETs, and BJT, including non-ideal effects.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Is able to describe the challenges of scaling of traditional MOSFETs and need for futuristic solid-state devices.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Is able to describe the operating principles, merits, demerits and challenges of some of the advanced solid-state devices.

lecture_topics: Basics of semiconductor physics: density of state, Fermi distribution function, semiconductor in equilibrium, dispersion relation
PN junctions: ideal behavior and non-ideal effects, capacitances, small signal equivalent circuit, breakdown
Metal-semiconductor junction: barrier height, rectifying and ohmic, Shottky barrier lowering, thermionic emission and tunneling
Field Effect Transistors: JFET, MESFET, and MOSFET
MOS Capacitor: fundamentals, band diagram, surface potential, inversion, flat voltage voltage, threshold voltage and its modeling
Parasitic charges in MOSFET: types and effects
MOSFET operation: input and output characteristics, saturation, transconductance, small signal model and frequency limitations
Non-ideal effects in MOSFETs: channel length modulation, velocity saturation, subthreshold current, DIBL, hot electron effects
BJT: structure, biasing, carrier profile, transistor action, current gain
BJT: Non-ideal effects: base width modulation, high-level injection, emitter bandgap narrowing, current crowding, breakdown
Introduction to device simulation, circuit simulation, and compact models
Scaling and limitations of traditional MOSFETs
Advanced MOSFETs: high-k gate dielectric, strained silicon and choice of channel material

resources.title: D. A. Neaman, "Semiconductor Physics and Devices"
Yannis Tsividis, “Operation and Modeling of the MOS Transistor”
Y. Taur and T.H. Ning, "Fundamentals of Modern VLSI Devices"
S. M. Sze & M. K. Lee, Semiconductor Devices, Physics and Technology
